## Summary

**STOREC** (Store Counted bytes from register into memory): Store at most "count" bytes from b into destination.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `b → <vea> with a maximum of count bytes` |
| Syntax | `STOREC b,count,<vea>` |
| Short | Store at most "count" bytes from b into destination |
| Description | It stores between 0 and 8 bytes of b depending on the count value. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–8 | d (count) |
| 2 | 7–0 | `00100100` |

- Count is a long, when negative there is no writing to memory.
- Count is ignored when destination is a register.
- Not allowed &lt;vea&gt; : #imm

### Example

```asm
    storec    d0,d1,(a2)
```

```text
b d0: 11 22 33 44 55 66 77 88
d d1: .. .. .. .. 00 00 00 03
Result:
```

- vea (a2) memory content where a2 points to

```text
11 22 33 .. .. .. .. ..
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no STOREC. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use an immediate `<vea>`.
